subject: OEM embedding: custody models, branding, and go/no-go criteria
messages:
From: Alden Cooper <alden@blueframe.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: OEM embed inquiry: Redwood in BlueFrame Assist

Hey Lauren —

Great meeting earlier. BlueFrame is exploring an OEM/white-label path for our Assist product and we think Redwood's inference platform would be a strong fit for embedding into our UI. High-level asks from our side:

- We need clarity on data custody models (hosted vs VPC vs on-prem) and what customer data stays in our control.
- Branding: how co-branded can the product be? Any restrictions on logos/marketing/legal mentions.
- Operational SLAs and telemetry: what level of tracing/telemetry is visible to us vs Redwood?
- Pricing model for embedded/volume commitments and any rebrand/license fees.

Timeline: goal is to decide technology approach by end of May and kick off a technical POC in June.

Can you share a short outline of custody options and a sample mutual action plan we could run against legal? Would like to loop in our legal lead (cc'd) if possible.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Alden Cooper
Head of Partnerships | BlueFrame
A: 415-555-0123

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: OEM embed inquiry: Redwood in BlueFrame Assist

Alden — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can absolutely move quickly here. Attached is a short primer that outlines three custody patterns we commonly offer and the tradeoffs for each. See attachment: redwood_oem_custody_options_v1.pdf

Quick summary (TL;DR):

1) Hosted OEM (Redwood-managed control plane, tenant isolation)
   - Fastest to ship, simplest commercial model (per-token + OEM uplift).
   - Data is encrypted at rest and in transit; customer data is logically isolated but keys are Redwood-managed.
   - Suitable when the partner wants minimal ops burden.

2) VPC/Private Control Plane (Control plane managed by Redwood but deployed in partner's VPC/account)
   - Customer manages cloud network and KMS; Redwood runs control plane components in their environment.
   - Better for regulated customers who require customer-managed keys and VPC peering.

3) Fully Private (On-prem / air-gapped)
   - Full data plane and control plane under customer control.
   - Strongest for privacy/regulatory needs; longer lead time and higher implementation cost.

Branding note: we support three levels of co-branding — \"Powered by Redwood\", white-label (no Redwood logo but product attribution in legal), and full OEM rebrand (custom UI assets).

Next steps I recommend:
- Share the primer with your legal/infra and confirm preferred custody model.
- I'll send a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for us to populate; if the VPC option is preferred we'll add an infra checklist.
- Proposed kickoff slots: Wed 5/12 — 9:00–10:30 PT or Thu 5/13 — 11:00–12:30 PT for a technical + legal sync.

Attaching: redwood_oem_custody_options_v1.pdf

LMK which slot works and I can send calendar invites.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OEM embed inquiry: Redwood in BlueFrame Assist (internal notes)

Internal notes and quick tech callouts before we lock messaging to BlueFrame:

- VPC/private-control-plane is the most likely recommended path for an ISV targeting enterprise customers; gives them KMS control and auditability while we can still push runtime updates under an agreed window.
- Telemetry: by default we anonymize token-level telemetry for hosted deployments; for VPC we can hand over richer telemetry (traces, request/response hashes) but we need an explicit data-sharing appendix to allow it. Suggest we default to request-level traces + redaction policy.
- Caching & model variants: if BlueFrame wants to ship with quantized small models to reduce cost, we can support that but need to agree on model pinning and fallback policies in the SLA.
- Legal: timeline for an MSA + DPA typically 3–4 weeks if both sides are responsive. If they push fully private, factor another 6–8 weeks for infra/config and security review.

Attaching brand guidelines for reference: redwood_branding_guidelines.png

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: draft MAP with VPC checklist and call out telemetry appendix.
- Aditya: prep a short infra playbook showing network/KMS requirements for VPC and on-prem.
- Lauren: propose kickoff window to Alden and include draft MAP.

-karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: OEM embedding — proposed approach and MAP

Alden / BlueFrame team —

Thanks for the quick responses and for looping legal. Based on our internal review we recommend pursuing the VPC / Private Control Plane model as the sensible default for BlueFrame: it balances speed-to-market with the key custody and telemetry controls enterprise customers expect.

What we propose now:

- Custody model: VPC + customer-managed KMS for key material. Redwood will deploy control-plane components into a BlueFrame-managed VPC (or partner account) with agreed maintenance windows.
- Telemetry: provide request-level traces and aggregated latency/cost metrics. No unredacted user messages will be shared by default. We'll include a telemetry appendix in the DPA.
- Branding: we can support OEM rebrand in the UI. Marketing/press needs to be coordinated but product UI can ship as fully white-labeled.

Attached: BlueFrame Mutual Action Plan (draft) — blueframe_mutual_action_plan.xlsx
Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C4D5E

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Legal: BlueFrame legal to review the MAP and confirm contact for MSA/DPA redlines (please reply with point-of-contact).
2) Technical kickoff: propose Mon 05/17 or Tue 05/18 for a 60–90 minute POC kickoff (we'll include infra and product owners).
3) MAP fill: Marissa will circulate a populated MAP in 24 hours with the VPC checklist included.

If that sounds good, please reply with legal contact and preferred kickoff date. We can put out a calendar next-day.

Attachments: blueframe_mutual_action_plan.xlsx
